questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The destination was pre-defined in my study program. I choose the program/track because of the academic area, but I was also excited about the location because I like the Italian language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Initially, the needed information was available, however, I faced a lot of bureaucratic/communication struggles when deciding to return to Denmark for the second semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome day where we met our teachers and got a tour of the campus so it was easy to find our classrooms once classes began.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was kind of difficult. I ended up booking an airbnb and living and two seperate ones for the duration of my stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I found it easy. Public transport in Milan works well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We could not send in our study plan to register for courses originally because of technical/administrative/bureaucratic issues. It meant that we had a chance to attend several classes and decide which to enroll in later, which was actually nice, but not intended. We also couldn't register for exams until shortly before because we hadn't been registered within the IT system.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We needed to fill out a pdf study plan and send it to our head of studies.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could only really email our head of studies or the universities administration whenever we hit a blockade that prevented us to register properly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed my classes, both the mandatory ones, which were most of them, but I was also happy that we could take electives in different faculties etc. I had a very nice elective in geology.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to reach out to the professors if you have doubts about lecture scheduling etc before registering.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were appropriate in my opinion. Some were repetitive compared to my courses on the bachelor, but others were more challenging because they were on a new topic.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH lectures are more interactive. In Milan it was mostly just the professor speaking for the entire lecture. It was really nice with lots of excursions in Milan though.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Laboratory in Sustainable Livestock Production
Laboratory in Sustainable Water Management
Laboratory in Sustainable Agricultural Mechanization
Geological Environments and Structures
Agricultural Systems and Soil Science
Italian level A1 (SLAM)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Laboratory in Sustainable Water Management was very appropriate within my programme and the exam project was a good way to use the knowledge in practice.
Geological Environments and Structures was super interesting and challenging if you haven't had geology before.
Agricultural Systems and Soil Science is good for repetition. but not a challenging course for natural science students who've had soil science before.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter additional unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was super expensive. Eating at restaurants/cafées and public transport was considerably cheaper than in DK. Grocery shopping was similar to DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We were not introduced to social activites at the university and din't really integrate with the other students there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to the gym, but not through the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking by Como/Lecco was super nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Italians are welcoming in my experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really since I didn't manage to do it. I lived with an Italian, which is the only thing I can recommend to immerse in the culture and get a local network.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Bureaucratic stuff taking ages and not getting clear directions on course registration, exams etc early on. And Italian showing up later, classes sometimes starting on time and sometimes not depending on the professor.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Cheap coffee, hospitality, great food and beautiful language that is fairly easy to understand.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look for housing early, have patience in terms of adminitrative parts and enjoy!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Challenging myself personally to push outside my comfort zone and explore a new culture, meet new people and have an open mind about new experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having a smaller social circle and not stressing out about the administrative stuff moving insanely slow so not being able to plan much in advance out of fear of not passing/getting my thesis approved etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
